Criterion: Findings are anchored to a specific, named detail
What pass requires: Passes when: every finding names a specific task, question, or feature in the lesson it is about. Fails when: a finding is stated with no specific task, question, or feature named.

Criterion: Cited statistics show their basis
What pass requires: Passes when: any statistic or count cited in a finding shows the calculation or source behind it. Fails when: a statistic is cited in a finding with no calculation or source shown.

Criterion: Substantive defect identified
What pass requires: Passes when: findings are ordered by substance, with real learning problems placed before surface-level issues like wording and formatting. Fails when: every finding addresses a surface-level issue like wording or formatting, with nothing on task design.

Criterion: Recommendations are specific to this lesson
What pass requires: Passes when: recommendation content could not be pasted unchanged onto a different lesson. Fails when: a recommendation is generic enough to paste onto another lesson unchanged.

Criterion: Named sources are supplied, not just referenced
What pass requires: Passes when: any source a recommendation names is supplied in the audit at usable length. Fails when: a recommendation names a source without supplying its text.

Criterion: Self-reported claims are verified, not echoed
What pass requires: Passes when: any claim the material makes about itself, such as a taught skill, a labeled standard, or a stated alignment, is tested against what students actually do. Fails when: a printed claim is echoed as fact without being checked against the actual task.

Criterion: Recommendation doesn't reintroduce a flagged gap
What pass requires: Passes when: a proposed fix is checked against every finding already raised in the same audit and does not recreate a gap already flagged elsewhere. Fails when: a fix recreates a gap the audit already flagged elsewhere.

Criterion: Verdict states the bottom line first
What pass requires: Passes when: the audit's single biggest finding appears in the first one to two sentences, before any analysis. Fails when: the bottom line appears only in the closing paragraph.

Criterion: A verdict-changing caveat is placed with the verdict
What pass requires: Passes when: any caveat that would change the verdict is stated next to the verdict itself. Fails when: a verdict-changing caveat appears only later in the document.

Criterion: Citations to source location are accurate
What pass requires: Passes when: any claimed location in the source material, such as a section, page, activity name, is confirmed against the actual document. Fails when: a location is inferred from a similarly named section rather than confirmed.

Criterion: Artifact creation is attempted
What pass requires: Passes when: the response includes at least one file-creation action for the audit. Fails when: no file-creation action appears anywhere in the response.

Criterion: Deliverable is a complete, exported artifact
What pass requires: Passes when: an attempted file is finished and saved as something a teacher could print or forward as-is. Fails when: an attempted file is left incomplete or is never saved.

Criterion: Deliverable is exported without requesting permission first
What pass requires: Passes when: a completed draft is saved and reported to the teacher directly. Fails when: the response asks the teacher whether to export a completed draft instead of exporting it.

Criterion: Findings are triaged by severity
What pass requires: Passes when: each finding is tagged with a stakes level such as confirm before teaching, flag for a coach conversation, minor. Fails when: all findings carry equal weight with no signal for which matters most.

Criterion: Teacher-facing tone
What pass requires: Passes when: the audit reads like a coach talking to a teacher, not a research memo or an adversarial critique. Fails when: the language reads academic or pointed enough that a teacher would need to translate it before repeating it.

Criterion: Tool-sourced claims aren't fabricated
What pass requires: Passes when: a specific fact that depends on a lookup, such as how a practice, DCI, or crosscutting concept officially pairs with a named standard, is only stated if a matching tool call, including a general web search, was actually made somewhere in the response. Fails when: a specific fact requiring a lookup is stated with confidence and no corresponding tool call of any kind appears anywhere in the transcript.

Criterion: Tool-sourced claims match what the tool returned
What pass requires: Passes when: a fact stated after a tool call traces directly to the content that tool actually returned. Fails when: a tool is called and returns an answer, but the written claim contradicts or misstates what came back.

Criterion: Fix resolves open structural questions
What pass requires: Passes when: a fix that touches a structural question, such as whether a task becomes required or stays optional, resolves it or explicitly flags it as an open decision for the teacher. Fails when: a fix changes how a task is used without saying whether it's now core or still optional.

Criterion: Fix includes a formative check for new tasks
What pass requires: Passes when: a fix that introduces a new task meant to build reasoning includes a quick way for the teacher to tell whether a student engaged with it. Fails when: a new reasoning task is added with no way to check whether a student reasoned through it or just repeated back a sample answer.

Criterion: Background section is scannable, not restated
What pass requires: Passes when: each sub-bullet in the background section adds information the teacher doesn't already have from an earlier sub-bullet. Fails when: the same standard, quote, or fact is restated across more than one sub-bullet before the findings begin.

Criterion: Retrieval limits are disclosed
What pass requires: Passes when: when materials are pulled from an external tool and the pull is incomplete, the audit states what it could not retrieve. Fails when: an audit built on a partial external pull doesn't mention the limitation anywhere.

Criterion: Lens coverage is disclosed
What pass requires: Passes when: the audit's background section names each required lens, alignment, instructional arc, rigor, access, and states whether it was examined. Fails when: a required lens is left unaddressed with no statement that it was skipped.

Criterion: Full audit is produced regardless of how the prompt is phrased
What pass requires: Passes when: a narrowly phrased teacher question still results in the standard audit and a saved artifact. Fails when: a narrow or conversational prompt causes the skill to answer only the literal question and skip the audit and artifact process.

Criterion: A missing matched external tool doesn't block the audit
What pass requires: Passes when: when no knowledge-graph tool matches the lesson's subject or standard, the audit still completes its findings using the lesson's own text and the standard's own language. Fails when: the absence of a matching tool is treated as a reason to skip a finding rather than a reason to reason from the source text directly.

Criterion: A lesson's own disclosed scope limit isn't written up as a finding
What pass requires: Passes when: a scope limitation the lesson's own materials state directly, such as a DCI deliberately deferred to a later lesson, is confirmed and left out of the findings list. Fails when: a lesson's own stated scope limitation is written up as a defect.

Criterion: A requested check the lesson misses becomes a finding
What pass requires: Every check the teacher asked about that the audit determines the lesson does not meet is written up as a finding with a fix. A check the teacher asked about counts even when it falls outside the lesson's stated objective, and an offer to write a fix later is not a fix.

Criterion: Fixes are summarized with their effort and impact
What pass requires: The audit includes one list or table that pairs every fix with the teacher time or effort it takes and how much it matters to the lesson. An audit that proposes no fixes passes. An offer to write fixes later is not a proposed fix, so an audit that only offers fixes counts as proposing none.

Criterion: The audit returns the lesson with its fixes made
What pass requires: The audit returns a revised version of the whole lesson, with every fix it proposes written in place and the sections no fix touches carried over unchanged. Revised excerpts of single sections do not count as the revised lesson. A fix that appears only in the findings, or only as an offer to revise later, is not in the revised lesson and does not count. An audit that proposes no fixes passes. An offer to write fixes later is not a proposed fix, so an audit that only offers fixes counts as proposing none.

Criterion: Changes in the revised lesson are marked
What pass requires: Every section the revision changes carries a mark that names the finding it carries out (e.g. "Revised · Finding 2"). An audit that returns no revised lesson passes; O12.33 scores that.

Criterion: The audit and the revised lesson are delivered as separate files
What pass requires: The response delivers the audit and the revised lesson as two separate files. An audit that returns no revised lesson passes; O12.33 scores that.

Criterion: The revised-lesson file holds only the lesson
What pass requires: The revised-lesson file holds the lesson ready to teach, with no findings or fix explanations in it. A change mark may name its finding and nothing more; a mark that says what changed or why counts as a fix explanation. An audit that returns no revised lesson passes; O12.33 scores that.

Criterion: Lesson-phase coherence
What pass requires: Passes when: opening, sequence, and closing are all addressed as one connected arc. Fails when: commentary clusters on one phase and skips the rest.

Criterion: Access barriers and proficiency range
What pass requires: Passes when: specific entry points, scaffolds, and extensions are named and preserve the learning target, with an extension named for a student who finishes early or already meets the target. Fails when: no extension for advanced students is named at all.

Criterion: Scaffolds and rigor-closing tasks are available to the whole class
What pass requires: Passes when: a task that closes a rigor gap is reachable by every student in the range, not gated to students who finish early. Fails when: a rigor-closing task is only available to students who finish other work early.

Criterion: Scaffold integrity
What pass requires: Passes when: no scaffold does the student's thinking for them. Fails when: a scaffold supplies most of the answer's content and isn't flagged as doing so.

Criterion: Social studies: inquiry chain builds toward the central question
What pass requires: Passes when: supporting questions build toward the central question, and every task has sources supplied. Fails when: a task has no sources and this is not flagged.

Criterion: Perspective integration isn't credited when only insiders disagree
What pass requires: Passes when: a claim of perspective integration requires at least one source from outside or affected by the decision being studied. Fails when: perspective integration is credited when only insiders disagree with each other.

Criterion: Proposed revisions are grade-band appropriate
What pass requires: Passes when: any new question or sample response written for a fix is checked against the lesson's grade band. Fails when: sample language is more sophisticated than a student at that grade would produce or understand.

Criterion: Worked examples, model answers, and keys are correct
What pass requires: The audit writes no worked example, model answer, expected answer, or answer key, or every one it writes is correct: each step is valid, the final answer is right, every claim it makes about why a step works is true, and every description it gives of a student's step or error matches the work it describes. Each one is checked on its own, even where the audit gets the same point right somewhere else.

Criterion: Simplifications don't teach rules that expire
What pass requires: No explanation or rule the audit writes for students, outside its worked examples and model or expected answers (P12.8 scores those), states something false. A claim that one step must come before another, or that a method is wrong, counts as a statement and is checked.

Criterion: Tasks the audit writes can be done as set up
What pass requires: Every task the audit writes for students can be done the way it is set up. Check every number, quantity, or comparison a task states, and every claim it makes about its own materials, against the task's own setup: no task asks students to do something its setup rules out, and no task describes its own setup falsely. An audit that writes no student tasks passes.

Criterion: ELA: explanatory reading
What pass requires: Passes when: at least one task requires explaining why something is true, not just locating or paraphrasing information. Fails when: accurate paraphrasing or vocabulary work is credited as mastery with no task requiring explanation.

Criterion: Math: reasoning and representation
What pass requires: Passes when: a task requires justifying or critiquing a method, and the lesson connects multiple representations of the same problem. Fails when: a lesson connects multiple representations but no task asks a student to justify a step or critique a method.

Criterion: Side-by-side methods are checked for a comparison task
What pass requires: Passes when: where a lesson places two methods side by side, a task asks why they agree or which is more efficient. Fails when: two methods are placed side by side with no task asking a student to compare them.

Criterion: Target alignment and cognitive rigor
What pass requires: Passes when: the audit states whether the material meets the full standard or only part of it, and checks the highest-demand task against the standard's required rigor. Fails when: partial alignment is claimed without naming what's missing.

Criterion: Missing targets are flagged, not assumed
What pass requires: Passes when: a lesson that cites no standard and states no objective is flagged as missing a target before any comparison is made. Fails when: the audit measures a lesson against a standard it silently assumed, with no target ever supplied by the lesson itself.

Criterion: Science: 3D sensemaking is named by content
What pass requires: Passes when: the practice, DCI, and crosscutting concept are each named by content rather than echoed as labels. Fails when: a label is echoed as well-structured without being tested against what students actually do.

Criterion: Science: safety notes are present for hands-on work
What pass requires: Passes when: safety notes accompany any hands-on investigation in the lesson. Fails when: a hands-on investigation has no accompanying safety guidance.

Criterion: Science: student-collected data is used as evidence
What pass requires: Passes when: data students generate themselves is used to support or challenge a claim. Fails when: data is shown to students with no task asking them to use it as evidence.

Criterion: The revision changes only what the findings name
What pass requires: Every change in the revised lesson carries out a fix the audit proposes. Parts of the lesson no finding names keep their original wording, order, and tasks. An audit that returns no revised lesson passes; O12.33 scores that.
